# Voice report D — entries #75–#97 (King Pungjang … Balhae)

Rewrites follow "Short and memorable": sentences under ~12 words, at most two proper nouns per sentence and three per paragraph. Where a rewrite drops a phrase that an image `at` points to, the entry is flagged **anchor**.

### King Pungjang (#75)
- **b0** (flashback title) — names: 5 (Eraha, Baekje, Seven-Branched Sword, Wa, + gloss 칠지도). Why it glazes: regnal number, a hanja gloss and a stiff "bestows… as a symbol of friendship".
  - Before: "The thirteenth Eraha of Baekje bestows the Seven-Branched Sword (칠지도) to the King of Wa, as a symbol of friendship."
  - After (EN): "A Baekje king sends the King of Wa a sword with seven branches. It is a gift. It is also a message."
  - After (KO): "백제의 임금이 왜왕에게 가지가 일곱 달린 칼을 보낸다. 선물이다. 전갈이기도 하다."
  - **anchor**: `chiljido-bestowal@bestows the Seven-Branched Sword` → retarget to "sword with seven branches".
- **b5** — names: 2 + a year + an age in parentheses (Baekje Revival Army). Why it glazes: textbook record ("in 661", "(35)", "from all around the world").
  - Before: "She dies the following year in 661. The eastern prince (35) takes the throne and forms the Baekje Revival Army. Baekje refugees gather from all around the world in order to restore Baekje."
  - After (EN): "She dies the next year. Her son takes the throne and keeps her promise. Baekje's refugees start coming home from everywhere they ran."
  - After (KO): "그녀는 이듬해 죽는다. 아들이 자리를 잇고, 어머니의 약속을 지킨다. 흩어졌던 백제 사람들이 도망친 곳곳에서 돌아오기 시작한다."
- **b6** — names: 10 (Pungjang, Gwishil Boksin, Hukchi Sangji, Satek Sangya, Bagon, Echi no Takutsu). Why it glazes: a cast card with an age gloss, right before a Roll Call scene that introduces every one of them better. Bagon never appears again. "Hukchi" is also spelled "Heukchi" two blocks later.
  - Before: "King Pungjang (37) · Gwishil Boksin · Hukchi Sangji · Satek Sangya · Bagon · Echi no Takutsu"
  - After (EN): cut the block. The Roll Call (b7–b30) does this job.
  - After (KO): 블록 삭제. 바로 뒤의 점호 장면이 같은 일을 한다.
- **b36–b37** — names: 4 (Pung, Revival Society, Pungjang, Boksin). Why it glazes: repeats b8 and b32 in file-card form ("the lead general of the Revival Society").
  - Before: "Prince Pung has been living in the East for over 20 years. He is the only prince left, so is welcomed as the leader of the Revival Society and crowned as King Pungjang. / Boksin, the lead general of the Revival Society, commands its armies — and begins to resent the king he crowned."
  - After (EN): cut b36. b37: "Pung was the only prince left, so they crowned him. Boksin did the crowning. Boksin is starting to regret it."
  - After (KO): b36 삭제. b37: "남은 왕자가 풍뿐이라 그를 왕으로 세웠다. 세운 사람은 복신이다. 복신은 그걸 후회하기 시작한다."
  - **anchor**: `pungjang-crowned@is welcomed as the leader of the Revival` → retarget to b37 "so they crowned him".
- **b41–b42** — names: 4 (Pung, Sand Fortress, Evasion Fortress, Silla). Why it glazes: translated fortress names that contradict the dialogue right after it (Juryu → Pisong), plus a ministry-minutes tone.
  - Before: "Prince Pung wants to move the base from Sand Fortress to the Evasion Fortress, against the advice of his ministers. / After 2 months, they're forced to move back because it is too close to the Silla border."
  - After (EN): b41: "Then Prince Pung wants to move house. The hill is barren, he says. The people will starve. Down on the plain there is rice." b42: "Two months later they move back up. The plain was a night's march from Silla."
  - After (KO): b41: "그러다 풍왕이 이사를 하겠다고 한다. 산은 메말랐다고. 백성이 굶을 거라고. 아래 들판에는 쌀이 있다고." b42: "두 달 뒤 그들은 다시 산으로 올라간다. 들판은 신라에서 하룻밤 거리였다."
  - **anchor**: `gwisil-bokshin@Prince Pung wants to move the base from` → "Then Prince Pung wants to move house".

### Pyongyang I (#76)
- **b0** — names: 1 (Red Sun). Why it glazes: art direction in the narration ("Every still of this city is that gate"), which the rule bans.
  - Before: "Red Sun's capital sits on the ridge — the red two-storey munru, the grey stone, the clouds that always look like weather about to choose a side. Every still of this city is that gate. There is no other capital."
  - After (EN): "Red Sun's capital sits on its ridge. A red two-storey gate, grey stone, and clouds that always look about to pick a side. There is only one gate anyone remembers."
  - After (KO): "붉은 해의 도성이 능선 위에 앉아 있다. 붉은 이층 문루, 회색 돌, 어느 편을 들지 막 정하려는 듯한 구름. 사람들이 기억하는 문은 그 하나뿐이다."
- **b7** — names: 6 (Yeon Namseng, Yalu, Qibi Heli, White Dragon). Why it glazes: a new Tang general's real name and his nickname in one breath.
  - Before: "In the ninth month Yeon Namseng holds the Yalu with several tens of thousands. The river freezes overnight. Qibi Heli, the White Dragon of the old war, walks his army across the ice at dawn…"
  - After (EN): "In the ninth month, Namseng holds the great river with tens of thousands. It freezes overnight. At dawn the White Dragon walks his army across the ice, drums going. He kills thirty thousand men guarding a river that is no longer there."
  - After (KO): "구월, 남생이 수만 군사로 큰 강을 지킨다. 강이 하룻밤 새 언다. 새벽, 백룡이 북을 울리며 군대를 얼음 위로 걸려 건넌다. 이제 거기 없는 강을 지키던 삼만이 베인다."
- **b10** — names: 6 (Surabol, Tang, Red Fowl, Munmu, Kim Yushin). Why it glazes: the first sentence spends two place names getting a letter from A to B.
  - Before: "In the twelfth month a letter reaches Surabol from the Tang camp. The Red Fowl is out of rice. King Munmu reads it out to his generals, and nobody offers, because everyone in the room knows…"
  - After (EN): "In the twelfth month, a letter comes down from the north. The Red Fowl is out of rice. Munmu reads it to his generals. Nobody offers. Everyone knows that road in winter. Kim Yushin, who is sixty-six, offers."
  - After (KO): "섣달, 북쪽에서 편지가 내려온다. 주작의 군량이 떨어졌다. 문무가 장수들 앞에서 읽는다. 아무도 나서지 않는다. 섣달의 북쪽 길이 어떤지 다들 안다. 예순여섯의 김유신이 나선다."

### Snake River (#77)
- **b0** — names: 8 (White Tiger, Snake River, Tang, Yeon Gesomun, Salsu, Yeon). Why it glazes: the Salsu aside brings in a second river while the reader is still meeting the first one.
  - Before: "The White Tiger drives into the Snake River with a Tang host that still believes rivers are roads. Yeon Gesomun has been waiting for a man who thinks that. Old men in the north still say Salsu…"
  - After (EN): "The White Tiger drives his host into the Snake River. They still believe rivers are roads. Yeon Gesomun has been waiting for a man who thinks that. Old men in the north remember another river that ate an army. The Snake is younger. It's hungrier. And it has Yeon's teeth."
  - After (KO): "백호가 군대를 몰아 사수로 들어온다. 그들은 아직 강을 길이라고 믿는다. 연개소문은 그렇게 믿는 자를 기다려 왔다. 북쪽 늙은이들은 군대를 삼킨 강을 하나 더 기억한다. 사수는 그보다 젊다. 더 굶주렸다. 그리고 연의 이빨을 가졌다."
  - **anchor**: `gesomun-samjogo-river@drives into the` → "drives his host into the".
- **b31** — names: 7 (Xue Rengui, Tianshan, Tiele, White Tiger II). Why it glazes: a mountain range and a steppe people the reader will never meet again.
  - Before: "The courier carrying the news finds Xue Rengui a thousand miles the other way, under the Tianshan, where he has just ended a war against the Tiele with three arrows…"
  - After (EN): "The courier finds Xue Rengui a thousand miles the other way. He has just ended a war in the far west with three arrows. His soldiers are already singing about it. He is given the dead man's title, White Tiger II. And the bill."
  - After (KO): "파발은 천 리 반대편에서 설인귀를 찾아낸다. 그는 서쪽 끝에서 화살 세 대로 전쟁 하나를 막 끝냈다. 병사들은 벌써 그 노래를 부른다. 그는 죽은 자의 이름을 받는다. 백호 2세. 그리고 그 셈도."

### Tamla Surrenders (#78)
- **b0** — names: 3 + a gloss (五, Sasu, Tamla). Why it glazes: a hanja numeral gloss and the Sino name for a river the reader knows as the Snake.
  - Before: "After the (五) Battle of Sasu, Tamla quietly changes sides."
  - After (EN): "After the Snake River, Tamla quietly changes sides."
  - After (KO): "사수의 싸움이 끝나자, 탐라는 조용히 편을 바꾼다."

### Rebellion (#79)
- **b1** — names: 4 + a year (Sabi, Baekje, Naesaji, Silla). Why it glazes: it opens well, then a year and a fort name stall it.
  - Before: "Two summers after Sabi, Baekje is supposed to be finished. Nobody has told the fortresses. In the eighth month of 662 the remnants gather at Naesaji, a hill fort east of the old capital…"
  - After (EN): "Two summers after Sabi, Baekje is supposed to be finished. Nobody has told the fortresses. The leftovers gather at a hill fort east of the old capital. They do what a kingdom does with no king nearby. They collect grain. They hang collaborators. They send boys to watch the Silla roads."
  - After (KO): "사비가 떨어지고 두 해 여름. 백제는 끝났어야 했다. 아무도 성들에게 그 말을 전하지 않았다. 남은 자들이 옛 도읍 동쪽의 산성에 모인다. 임금이 곁에 없는 나라가 하는 일을 한다. 곡식을 걷는다. 부역자를 매단다. 신라 길목에 소년들을 세워 망을 보게 한다."
- **b2** — names: 11 (Munmu, Kim Jinju, Grand General of the Tang Army Command, True Bone, Yellow Mountain, Chang'an). Why it glazes: an office string, then three appositives about one man.
  - Before: "Munmu names nineteen generals to deal with it. One of them is Kim Jinju, Grand General of the Tang Army Command, a True Bone of good family who led men at the Yellow Mountain and has a son…"
  - After (EN): "Munmu names nineteen generals for it. One of them is Kim Jinju. He is True Bone, from a good family. He led men at the Yellow Mountain. He has a son in the emperor's guard."
  - After (KO): "문무는 이 일에 장군 열아홉을 붙인다. 그중 하나가 김진주다. 좋은 집안의 진골이다. 황산벌에서 군사를 이끌었다. 아들 하나가 황제의 숙위로 가 있다."
- **b10** — names: 7 (Jinju, Suse, Hanseong, Tang, Baekje, Naesaji, Silla). Why it glazes: a governor and a city that exist only to footnote a clerical error.
  - Before: "The annals are not finished with him. Eight years later the same pages have a Jinju sent to behead Suse, governor of Hanseong, who was caught arranging to go over to the Tang commandery in Baekje…"
  - After (EN): "The annals aren't done with him. Eight years later, the same pages send a Jinju to behead a traitor governor. Later tellers like that version better. They even give him the credit for this hill fort. Either Silla had two men of the name, or a clerk killed him once and forgot. Only one person never mixes them up: his son."
  - After (KO): "연대기는 아직 그를 놓아주지 않는다. 여덟 해 뒤, 같은 책은 진주라는 사내를 보내 배신한 총관의 목을 베게 한다. 뒷날의 이야기꾼들은 그쪽이 더 좋다. 이 산성을 꺾은 공까지 그에게 돌린다. 신라에 그 이름이 둘이었거나, 서기가 그를 한 번 죽여 놓고 잊었거나. 판본을 한 번도 헷갈리지 않는 사람은 하나뿐이다. 그의 아들."

### Betrayal (#80)
- **b1** — names: 6 (Boksin, Juryu, Sabi, Spirit Army, Tang, Dochim). Why it glazes: one long sentence carries a founding, a place, a season, a costume change and a title.
  - Before: "Before Boksin and the king there were Boksin and the monk. Dochim raised the first restoration banner at Juryu with him in the autumn Sabi fell, a monk who put down the begging bowl for a spear…"
  - After (EN): "Before Boksin and the king, there were Boksin and the monk. Dochim raised the first banner with him, the autumn Sabi fell. He put down his begging bowl for a spear. He named himself General of the Spirit Army. For a year the two held the west between them. The enemy garrison couldn't even go out for water."
  - After (KO): "복신과 왕 이전에, 복신과 승려가 있었다. 사비가 떨어진 가을, 도침이 그와 함께 첫 깃발을 들었다. 바리때를 내려놓고 창을 든 승려였다. 스스로 영군장군이라 불렀다. 한 해 동안 둘은 서쪽을 나눠 쥐었다. 적의 수비대는 물 길으러도 못 나왔다."

### White River (#81)
- **b3** — names: 9 (Liu Rengui, Black Tortoise, Baekje, Ungjin, Sun Renshi, Yellow Sea, Silla). Why it glazes: real name plus nickname plus capital plus a second general plus a sea, all before the joke lands.
  - Before: "Count the banners before the water does. Tang comes by sea, twice. Liu Rengui, the Black Tortoise, has held the old Baekje capital at Ungjin for two winters with a garrison too small to be called one…"
  - After (EN): "Count the banners before the water does. Tang comes by sea, twice. The Black Tortoise has held the old capital for two winters with a garrison too small to deserve the word. The emperor wrote that he could come home. He wrote back that he'd rather not. So in spring the emperor sends him seven thousand more. The Silla annals, which like round numbers, make it four hundred thousand."
  - After (KO): "깃발부터 세자. 물이 세기 전에. 당은 바다로, 두 번 온다. 현무는 수비대라 부르기도 민망한 병력으로 옛 도성을 두 겨울째 지키고 있다. 황제가 돌아와도 좋다고 썼다. 그는 차라리 남겠다고 답했다. 그래서 봄에 황제는 칠천을 더 보낸다. 둥근 숫자를 좋아하는 신라의 사서는 그것을 사십만이라 적는다."
- **b8** — names: 7 (Juryu, Pungjang, Silla, Tang, Echi no Takutsu, Kudara). Why it glazes: a nested source-criticism aside ("by the count Silla will later send the Tang") inside a dash clause.
  - Before: "Upriver at Juryu, King Pungjang still believes a kingdom can be restored by enough sails. Over three summers the East has sent him a thousand ships, by the count Silla will later send the Tang…"
  - After (EN): "Upriver, King Pungjang still believes enough sails can restore a kingdom. For three summers the East has sent him ships. A thousand, if you trust the enemy's count. Forty-two thousand men. Takutsu is among the captains who still say Kudara. They come down on the eighth month's water, packed too tight to row. They are shouting for a victory the tide has already priced differently."
  - After (KO): "상류에서 풍장왕은 아직, 배만 넉넉하면 나라를 되찾을 수 있다고 믿는다. 세 해 여름 동안 동쪽은 배를 보내 주었다. 적의 셈을 믿는다면 천 척이다. 군사는 사만 이천. 다쿠쓰도 그 장수들 사이에 있다. 아직 쿠다라라고 부르는 사람들이다. 그들은 노를 젓지도 못할 만큼 빽빽하게 팔월의 물을 타고 내려온다. 밀물이 이미 다른 값을 매긴 승리를 외치면서."
  - **anchor**: `takutsu-kinshi-prow@Echi no Takutsu among the captains` → "Takutsu is among the captains".
- **b19** — names: 14 (Sun Renshi, Liu Renyuan, Silla, Juryu, Black Tortoise, Ungjin, White River, Du Shuang, Buyeo Yung). Why it glazes: a staff roster. Three Tang generals the reader never meets again.
  - Before: "So the armies divide. Sun Renshi, Liu Renyuan and the king of Silla take the land road to Juryu. The Black Tortoise takes the water: a hundred and seventy warships and the grain boats, down the Ungjin river…"
  - After (EN): "So the armies split. Most of the generals take the land road. The Black Tortoise takes the water: a hundred and seventy warships, heading for the river mouth. On his deck stands Buyeo Yung."
  - After (KO): "그래서 군은 갈라진다. 장수들 대부분은 뭍길을 탄다. 현무는 물을 맡는다. 전선 백칠십 척이 하구를 향해 내려간다. 그 갑판 위에 부여융이 서 있다."
- **b23** — names: 4 (Black Tortoise, White River, Kim Yushin). Why it glazes: a colon list chained into one sentence. The nouns are fine; the shape isn't.
  - Before: "The Black Tortoise has already learned the river's grammar: narrow mouth, sandbars that shift like lies, a current that punishes anyone who charges without forming line. He anchors a hundred and seventy ships…"
  - After (EN): "The Black Tortoise has already learned the river's grammar. A narrow mouth. Sandbars that shift like lies. A current that punishes anyone who charges out of line. He anchors his hundred and seventy ships across the throat and waits. On the east bank, Kim Yushin's army keeps the shore from becoming a pier."
  - After (KO): "현무는 이미 강의 문법을 배웠다. 좁은 하구. 거짓말처럼 움직이는 모래톱. 대열 없이 덤비는 자를 벌하는 물살. 그는 백칠십 척을 목구멍에 가로질러 닻을 내리고 기다린다. 동쪽 기슭에서는 김유신의 군대가 그 기슭이 부두가 되지 않게 막는다."
- **b33** — names: 6 (Black Tortoise, Wa, Luoyang, Middle Kingdom). Why it glazes: 122 words, and the guesthouse anecdote is one sentence with three clauses.
  - Before: "The Black Tortoise has seen men of Wa once before, four years ago in Luoyang: an embassy in court silk that bowed in all the right places, and that the court then kept in a guesthouse for two winters…"
  - After (EN): "The Black Tortoise has seen men of Wa once before, in the emperor's city. They were envoys in court silk, and they bowed in all the right places. The court kept them in a guesthouse for two winters, so they couldn't carry home where the fleet was going. These are their cousins. They row standing up. They shout from too far away. They charge a hundred and seventy anchored hulls in boats built for rice. Nobody in his army has fought them before. He watches the first wave break on his line like a scholar reading a new script. He is looking for the grammar."
  - After (KO): "현무는 왜인을 한 번 본 적이 있다. 황제의 도성에서였다. 비단 조복을 입은 사신들이었고, 절할 자리마다 꼬박꼬박 절했다. 조정은 그들을 두 겨울 동안 객관에 붙잡아 두었다. 함대가 어디로 가는지 고국에 전하지 못하게. 지금 저들은 그 사신들의 사촌쯤 된다. 선 채로 노를 젓는다. 소용없는 거리에서 고함을 지른다. 쌀 나르는 배로, 닻 내린 백칠십 척에 곧장 달려든다. 그의 군대에서 이들과 싸워 본 사람은 없다. 그는 첫 물결이 전열에 부서지는 것을 지켜본다. 처음 보는 글자를 읽는 학자처럼. 문법을 찾으면서."
- **b70** — names: 13 (Imjon, Ji Subsin, Silla, Baekje, Heukchi Sangji, Satek Sangya, Boksin, Tang, Black Tortoise, Sun Renshi). Why it glazes: a new commander, two known generals with full clan names, three kingdoms and a dissenting general, all in four sentences.
  - Before: "One fortress does not hear it. At Imjon, Ji Subsin shuts the gate and holds through the autumn, and Silla's siege breaks on it and goes home in the eleventh month. It falls in the end to Baekje hands…"
  - After (EN): "One fortress doesn't hear it. Its commander shuts the gate and holds all autumn, and the siege goes home. In the end it falls to its own people's hands. Sangji and Sangya have changed sides. The Black Tortoise hands back their armour and points them up the slope."
  - After (KO): "한 성만은 그 말을 듣지 않는다. 성주는 문을 닫고 가을 내내 버티고, 포위군은 돌아간다. 결국 그 성은 제 나라 사람 손에 떨어진다. 상지와 상여가 편을 바꾼 것이다. 현무는 그들에게 갑옷을 돌려주고 비탈 위를 가리킨다."
  - **dependency**: b72 then needs "Ji Subsin" → "The commander" ("The commander leaves his wife and children inside and goes north…" / "성주는 처자식을 성 안에 두고 북쪽 고구려로 간다…").

### Yeon Gesomun† (#82)
- **b12** — names: 2 + a number (Wang Geon, Goryeo, "250 years"). Why it glazes: names a future founder and spends a mystery box in a clause.
  - Before: "Yeon catches a vision of Wang Geon, the man who will revive Goryeo 250 years after his death."
  - After (EN): "Yeon catches a vision of something at the very end. A young man, centuries off, saying Goryeo as if it had never gone."
  - After (KO): "마지막 순간, 연의 눈앞에 무언가가 스친다. 몇백 년 뒤의 젊은 사내 하나가, 사라진 적 없다는 듯 고려라는 이름을 입에 올린다."
- **b15** — names: 2 + age gloss + office (Yeon Namseng, Supreme Commander). Why it glazes: the file-card form "X (31), his eldest son, takes on the title of Y".

  - Before: "In 674 the Third Emperor strips King Munmu of every Tang title and names a new king of Silla: Kim Inmun, Munmu's younger brother, who has lived in Chang'an since he was a young man of twenty-two…"
  - After (EN): "The Third Emperor takes back every title he ever gave Munmu. Then he names a new king: Munmu's little brother, Inmun. Inmun has lived in the emperor's city since he was twenty-two. An official has to tell him he's going home. With an army."
  - After (KO): "황제는 문무에게 준 관작을 모두 거둬들인다. 그리고 새 왕을 세운다. 문무의 아우, 인문이다. 인문은 스물둘부터 황제의 도성에서 살아 왔다. 고국에 간다는 말을 관리에게서 들어야 한다. 군대를 데리고."
- **b3** — names: 6 (Liu Rengui, Black Tortoise, Silla, Chang'an, Tang). Why it glazes: real name and nickname together, then two place names in the payoff.
  - Before: "Liu Rengui, the Black Tortoise, is given the army. Inmun is given the title, a new robe in the Silla colour, and a seat in the general's ship that faces backwards, toward Chang'an…"
  - After (EN): "The Black Tortoise gets the army. Inmun gets the title, a new robe in his country's colour, and a seat on the general's ship. It faces backwards, toward the capital. The clerks are very particular about where a puppet sits."
  - After (KO): "군대는 현무에게 간다. 인문에게는 칭호와 제 나라 빛깔의 새 도포, 그리고 장군의 배 위 자리 하나가 주어진다. 그 자리는 뒤를 본다. 황제의 도성 쪽이다. 서기들은 꼭두각시가 어디 앉는지에 무척 까다롭다."

### Maeso (#94)
- **b1** — names: 6 (Xue Rengui, Silla, Kim Punghun, Munmu, Tang). Why it glazes: a dash clause carries the whole reveal.
  - Before: "Xue Rengui comes back by sea in the ninth month, with a Silla man named Kim Punghun as his pilot — the son of a man Munmu executed, showing the Tang fleet the way into his own coast."
  - After (EN): "Xue Rengui comes back by sea in the ninth month. His pilot is Kim Punghun. Munmu killed his father. Now the son is showing the enemy fleet the way into his own coast."
  - After (KO): "설인귀가 아홉째 달에 바다로 돌아온다. 길잡이는 김풍훈이다. 문무가 그의 아버지를 죽였다. 이제 그 아들이 적의 함대에게 제 나라 해안으로 드는 길을 일러 준다."
- **b16** — names: 4 (Maeso, Li Jinxing, Mohe, Imjin). Why it glazes: a one-off Tang general's name stalls the best joke in the entry.
  - Before: "The army at Maeso is Li Jinxing's, and it is mostly Mohe, and the Mohe are mostly horse. Thirty thousand of them graze the flats under the walls, because the grass is outside…"
  - After (EN): "The army at Maeso is mostly Mohe, and the Mohe are mostly horse. Thirty thousand of them graze the flats under the walls. The grass is outside. No fortress on that river was built to stable a herd."
  - After (KO): "매소성의 군대는 대부분 말갈이고, 말갈은 대부분 말이다. 삼만 필이 성벽 아래 들판에서 풀을 뜯는다. 풀은 성 밖에 있다. 그 강가의 어떤 성도 그만한 무리를 들이도록 지어지지 않았다."

### Final Ford (#95)
- **b0** — names: 4 (Protectorate, Pyongyang, Liaodong, Xue Rengui). Why it glazes: an administrative relocation told as an itinerary.
  - Before: "In the second month the Protectorate headquarters is moved out of Pyongyang to Liaodong, then further, and then it stops being mentioned. Xue Rengui still has a fleet, and a fleet does not need a headquarters."
  - After (EN): "In the second month, the emperor's headquarters quietly leaves Pyongyang. Then it moves further. Then nobody mentions it. Xue still has a fleet, and a fleet doesn't need a headquarters."
  - After (KO): "이월, 황제의 도호부가 슬그머니 평양을 떠난다. 그러고는 더 멀리 간다. 그러고는 아무도 입에 올리지 않는다. 설인귀에게는 아직 함대가 있고, 함대에는 도호부가 필요 없다."

### The King for All (#96)
- **b4** — names: 2 + age gloss + title (Munhee, Queen Munmyung). Why it glazes: the age tag and a new royal name come before the image, which is a mother fixing a collar.
  - Before: "Munhee (70) — Queen Munmyung now, and the last person alive who remembers all of it from the inside — is straightening her son's collar. She was twenty-six when this story started…"
  - After (EN): "Munhee is seventy. She is the last person alive who remembers all of it from the inside, and she is straightening her son's collar. She was twenty-six when this story started. Her sister burned a skirt on a hill so that she could be married."
  - After (KO): "문희는 일흔이다. 이 모든 일을 안에서 기억하는 마지막 사람이고, 지금은 아들의 옷깃을 여며 주고 있다. 이야기가 시작될 때 그는 스물여섯이었다. 언니가 언덕에서 치마를 태운 덕에 혼인할 수 있었다."
  - **anchor**: `two-kings-crowns@Queen Munmyung now, and the last person` → "the last person alive who remembers" (shared with `thrones-succession-blue`).

### Balhae (#97)
- **b30** — names: 2 (Sanggyeong, Mudanjiang). Why it glazes: it reads like a shot list ("a stamped grid of halls — lotus tiles, a stone lantern") with no sentence around it.
  - Before: "Sanggyeong is later a stamped grid of halls on the Mudanjiang — lotus tiles, a stone lantern."
  - After (EN): "His capital will be a stamped grid of halls on the Mudanjiang. Lotus tiles. A stone lantern. Nobody there will need telling what the old country was called."
  - After (KO): "그의 도성은 무단강가에 찍힌 궁성의 격자가 될 것이다. 연꽃 와당. 석등 하나. 그곳 사람들에게 옛 나라의 이름을 일러 줄 필요는 없을 것이다."
- No card: this is the last entry. The era line (b31) and "THE END" stay.

No flagged or clogged narration in: *Stone Gate* (#89), *Wonsul* (#90), *The Wanggeom's Guest* (#92). Their problems are elsewhere: *Wanggeom's Guest* b8 has a profanity and an inner monologue in the narration, which is a voice choice and not a name problem.

## Five worst paragraphs in this range
1. **White River b19** — 14 names. A Tang staff roster where the reader needs only "the Black Tortoise takes the water, Yung on deck."
2. **White River b70** — 13 names in four sentences, including a new commander who exists for two blocks.
3. **Mount Gain b1** — 11 names plus a year, all hung off Buyeo Yung as appositives.
4. **Rebellion b2** — an office string ("Grand General of the Tang Army Command") plus three appositives about a man who matters only for calling in sick.
5. **King Pungjang b41–b42** — translated fortress names ("Sand Fortress", "Evasion Fortress") that contradict the Juryu/Pisong dialogue right after them, in textbook tense.

## Names that should be wiki-only (never on the page)
- **Tang staff:** Sun Renshi, Liu Renyuan, Du Shuang, Qibi Heli (keep "the White Dragon"), Li Jinxing. Use "Liu Rengui" only as a speaker id; on the page he is the Black Tortoise.
- **One-off people:** Bagon, Jinheum, Suse, Jipdeuk, Yomyo, Ji Subsin (say "the commander"), Imyun (fine as a speaker label, never in narration).
- **Future founders before their time:** Wang Geon and Gung Ye. They spend the "Goguryeo never dies" payoff.
- **Places that are only route-map:** Tianshan, Tiele, Hanseong, Naesaji, Chwirisan (keep the translated "Mountain Where One Goes for Gain"), Geumma, Bodeok, Paegak, Gunghol, Liaodong, Nangnang, the Four Commanderies, Salsu (in *Snake River*), and the translated "Sand Fortress" / "Evasion Fortress".
- **Glosses and sources:** 칠지도, (五), 신단수 inside the English, "Eraha", and "the Samguk Yusa counts".
